title: Invertibility of canonical strict-local cube stalk restrictions
statement: Let S,T,X,X' be schemes [def-pc-scheme], f:X→S quasi-compact (the inverse image of every affine open is quasi-compact) and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], and (g':X'→X,f':X'→T,f,g:T→S) a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Let k,k' be separably closed fields, Ω an algebraically closed field, σ:Spec k→S, τ:Spec k'→T, ι:Spec k'→Spec k, ν:Spec Ω→Spec k', with ι≫σ=τ≫g [def-weil-geometric-point]. Let A,B be strictly henselian local rings [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], eA:Spec A≅S_(νισ), eB:Spec B≅T_(ντ) [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and put jA=eA≫j_(νισ), jB=eB≫j_(ντ), using the structural maps [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map]. Let φ:A→B be local and ρA:Spec k→Spec κA, ρB:Spec k'→Spec κB satisfy Spec φ≫jA=jB≫g, ρA≫rA≫jA=σ, ρB≫rB≫jB=τ, and ρB≫Spec(κφ)=ι≫ρA, where rA,rB are the residue closed-point maps and κφ is the induced residue-field map. Choose X₀ with maps p₀:X₀→X and f₀:X₀→Spec A making a cartesian square over f,jA; choose X₁ with maps p₁:X₁→X₀ and f₁:X₁→Spec B making a cartesian square over f₀,g₀=Spec φ. For an abelian etale sheaf G on X [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] and q∈ℕ put G₀=p₀^*G, K=G[0], K₀=G₀[0], with exact derived inverse image [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image] and derived direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Let C₁=H^q(g^*Rf_*K), C₂=H^q(Rf'_*g'^*K), L₁=H^q(g₀^*Rf₀_*K₀), L₂=H^q(Rf₁_*p₁^*K₀). Let e:C₁→C₂ and e₀:L₁→L₂ be homology of the two derived exchange maps [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange], and t₀:Spec κB→Spec B the closed point. Additionally choose b:X1->X' such that b g'=p1 p0 and (b,f1,f',jB) is cartesian. Use the explicit derived comparison maps u1,u2 of [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exchange-cube-comparisons], and put t=rB rhoB:Spec k'->Spec B. The point equation identifies t jB with tau. The induced homology stalk maps r1:(H^q M1)_tau -> (H^q N1)_t and r2:(H^q M2)_tau -> (H^q N2)_t are isomorphisms. This asserts only invertibility of the two fixed restriction maps, with no assertion about exchange or its compatibility.
